title: How Sink Drainage Works: Gravity, Venting, and Traps
description: Sink drainage relies on a coordinated system of gravity, venting, and liquid seals. When water leaves the sink basin, it passes through the trap, which retains a small amount of water to block sewer gases from entering the living space. Downstream of the trap, the drainage pipe connects to a vent stack that introduces atmospheric air into the system. This balance of pressure prevents air locks and ensures smooth, rapid discharge without siphoning the trap dry. Understanding this mechanical interaction helps technicians diagnose gurgling sounds, slow drainage, and unpleasant odors effectively.
